paper.title: Accelerating materials property prediction via a hybrid Transformer Graph framework that leverages four body interactions
paper.research_summary: We propose a framework utilizing a Graph Neural Network with composition-based and crystal structure-based architectures, combined with a transfer learning scheme. This approach accurately predicts energy-related properties (e.g., total energy, energy above the convex hull, energy band gap) and data-scarce mechanical properties (e.g., bulk and shear modulus). Our model incorporates four-body interactions, capturing periodicity and structural characteristics. It outperforms state-of-the-art models in 8 materials property regression tasks.

tasks.objective: accurately predict energy-related properties (e.g., total energy, energy above the convex hull, energy band gap) and data-scarce mechanical properties (e.g., bulk and shear modulus)
constraints: capturing global crystal structure and periodicity information
output_goal: property predictions with high accuracy and generalization capability

evidence.text: This approach accurately predicts energy-related properties (e.g., total energy, energy above the convex hull, energy band gap) and data-scarce mechanical properties (e.g., bulk and shear modulus).

evidence.text: To convert a crystal structure into a graph representation, we employ a unique approach aimed at encapsulating the essential structural characteristics while minimizing the computational complexity... three distinct graphs are generated to encode a single crystal structure: the original atomic graph G8 its corresponding line graph L(G8), and the dihedral graph L(G8d).

evidence.text: Model architecture for crystal structure... Our compositional model comprises two primary modules. The initial module is a transformer-based architecture... The second module is DenseNet... Model training for both parallel architectures is the single training process.

stages.stage_goal: fine-tune pre-trained model on data-scarce secondary properties (mechanical, dielectric, vibrational)

evidence.text: To overcome the challenge of data scarcity, we employed TL techniques to leverage existing knowledge and enhance the performance of our model. By pretraining the model on a large-scale dataset of DFT computed formation energies, we were able to leverage the learned representations and fine-tune the model (CrysCoT).
evidence.section: Transfer learning for data-scarce material properties

evidence.text: To benchmark CrysCo’s performance, we used 8 properties datasets (Table 1) that include material compositions, crystal structures, and tabulated physical and chemical descriptors as inputs... Table 2 compares the mean absolute error (MAE) of CrysCo and CrysGNN models predictions with the MEGNet17, CGCNN18, SchNet20, ALIGNN21, Matformer29, and DeeperGATGNN37 baselines for all 8 datasets.

stages.stage_name_raw: predicting properties of novel in-house DFT-relaxed structures
stages.stage_goal: validate generalization capability on unseen crystalline materials
stage_input: novel structures generated and DFT-relaxed in-house
stage_output: predicted Ef and EHull values with Pearson correlation coefficients

evidence.text: To further investigate the performance of our model, we applied CrysCo to predict Ef and EHull of materials from a new dataset containing 751 novel structures generated and DFT-relaxed in-house. Parity plots in the supplementary Figure S1 shows good agreement between predicted and calculated energy values, with Pearson correlation coefﬁcients equal to 0.894 (Ef) and 0.931 (EHull).
In order to evaluate the performance of our hybrid model (CrysCo), for training and testing purposes we used DFT-calculated solid-state properties from the MP21 database4.
To benchmark CrysCo’s performance, we used 8 properties datasets (Table 1) that include material compositions, crystal structures, and tabulated physical and chemical descriptors as inputs.
